data.segment_title: Preview/Introduction Tom Brokaw (Republican National Convention in New York)

data.segment_description:
(New York: Tom Brokaw) Report introduced. 
 (Moscow: Dawna Friesen) The hostage situation in Beslan, Russia, where terrorists wearing suicide bomb belts are holding hundreds of hostages, including children, featured; scenes shown of Russian troops and worried family members outside the school; details given about recent terror attacks involving rebels from Chechnya and of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s vow not to negotiate with terrorists. [Russian Defense Minister Sergei IVANOV† {thru translator}&nbsp- says war has been declared on us.] [Former Chechen presidential candidate Malik SAIDULLAYEV† {thru translator} – says the things that are happening in Chechnya are coming back into Russia.] [Carnegie Moscow Center terrorism analyst Alexey MALASHENKO†- states the Chechen conflict is spreading.]

(New York: Tom Brokaw) The deaths of civilians in a US air strike on Fallujah, Iraq; an assassination attempt on Iraqi National Congress leader Ahmed Chalabi; the release of 7 hostages, and the reopening of Iraqi oil pipelines reported.

(New York: Tom Brokaw) Day 3 of the Republican National Convention in New York, where Vice President Dick Cheney and Democratic Senator Zell Miller will speak, noted. 
 (Convention floor: Brian Williams) The convention featured; details given of Miller’s decision to back the Republicans; scenes shown of last night’s proceedings and the interruption of a speech by White House chief of staff Andrew Card by protestors during a youth event. [In July, 1992, MILLER – speaks against then-candidate George Bush and the Republicans.] [Last night, California Governor Arnold SCHWARZENEGGER – warns against being “economic girlie men.”] [Last night, daughter Jenna BUSH, First Lady Laura BUSH – speak at the convention.] 
 (New York: Campbell Brown) Cheney as a liability for the presidential campaign featured; NBC News/"Wall Street Journal" poll results cited; details given of controversies over his connection to Halliburton and his assertions about ties between Iraqi President Saddam Hussein and Al Qaeda. [Earlier, wife Lynne CHENEY – calls Dick the grandfather of the US.] [Pollster Andrew KOHUT†- says all of the criticism sticks to Cheney.] [Republican strategist Kenneth DUBERSTEIN†- comments on Cheney’s low visibility after the September 11 attacks.] [Last June & December, 2001, CHENEY – makes contradictory statements about a meeting between an Iraqi official and a 9/11 hijacker.] [Former Senator Alan SIMPSON††- calls Cheney unflappable.] 
 (New York: Tom Brokaw) Report introduced. 
 (New York: Tom Costello) The protests in New York against President Bush’s policies featured; arrest figures cited; scenes shown. [Protestor Myra BRONSTEIN‡- says Bush’s administration has been a nightmare for working people.] [Presidential historian Douglas BRINKLEY†- predicts the intensity of the protests & the division is going to increase.] [New York resident Dave RIO‡- says it’s the same thing over & over.]

data.segment_title: In Depth (Decision 2004 / Bush vs. Kerry / Kerry)
data.segment_description:
(New York: Tom Brokaw) Senator John Kerry’s break with tradition to speak at an event during the Republicans’ convention noted. 
 (Nashville, Tennessee: Carl Quintanilla) Kerry’s efforts to counter worries that his campaign has been slow to respond to attacks and leisurely in its image featured; scenes shown of Kerry windsurfing; details given of suggestions that Kerry should steer away from talking about the war. [Before the American Legion in Nashville, KERRY – refutes President Bush’s remarks that the war on terror is not winnable.] [Representative Charles RANGEL†- says we have to fight as though the security of our country depends on it.] [Democratic pollster Peter HART††- says Kerry is on the offensive when he’s talking about the economy & health care.] [Navy veteran John NEYLON†- says he doesn’t trust Kerry.] [In Pennsylvania, Senator John EDWARDS – criticizes Republicans.] 
 (New York: Tom Brokaw) The defeat of Palm Beach County, Florida, Elections Supervisor Theresa LePore in yesterday’s election noted.

 (Pentagon: Jim Miklaszewski) The FBI’s investigation into spying at the Pentagon reviewed; details given of the focus on Israeli diplomat Naor Gilon†, who may have ties to pro-Israel lobby group AIPAC and Pentagon analyst Lawrence Franklin, suspected of passing information about Iran. [Israeli embassy spokesman David SIEGEL†- denies the allegations.] [Former U.N. weapons inspector David ALBRIGHT†- comments on Israel’s fear that the US won’t be tough enough in halting weapons production by Iran.]

data.segment_description: (New York: Tom Brokaw) Report introduced.   (New York: Anne Thompson) College crackdowns on students who download music from the Internet illegally featured; statistics cited. [University of Minnesota student Mike REYNOLDS††- says a lot of people do it.] [Forrester Research media analyst Josh BERNOFF†- explains why downloading music is prevalent at colleges.] [University of Minnesota chief information officer Steve CAWLEY†- says education is our primary means of dealing with it.] [University of Florida Rob BIRD††- describes Icarus, a program he wrote to uncover illegal downloading and restrict students’ Internet access if detected.]
